description: The Cassini ISS narrow-angle camera is an f/10.5 reflecting telescope with a 0.35 by 0.35 degree field of view, a spectral range of 200 to 1100 nm, and two filter wheels that carry 12 filters each.
short_description: Cassini ISS narrow-angle camera filters and filter combinations
facility_description: Cassini-Huygens launched on 15 October 1997 and the orbiter entered Saturn orbit on 1 July 2004; the Imaging Node portal describes later Equinox and Solstice extensions through September 2017.
notes: Band Comments quote central wavelength, FWHM and effective wavelength from Table A.2 of Knowles, Cassini ISS Data User's Guide, 16 September 2018, on the PDS Imaging Node. Those rows are calibration products in a NASA PDS document, so the NASA Science Data Portal CC0 statement is applied to them. The Kluwer/Springer Porco et al. 2004 PDF is cited as the instrument paper and as the source that publishes Table VIII and transmission figures; its numeric tables were not copied into these Comments because that PDF states it was printed by Kluwer Academic Publishers. NJM single-filter names are the Table A.2 pair of that filter with CL1 or CL2. NJM two-filter names are the Table A.2 pairs that the guide actually lists. Table A.2 also lists NAC RED/IR3 and WAC IR3/RED and WAC IR3/IR1, which are not NJM keys and are omitted. Polarizers (NAC P0, P60, P120, IRP0; WAC IRP0, IRP90) are described in the user guide and instrument catalogs but are not NJM band names. CB1a and CB1b are the two peaks of the CB1 response, not separate filters. Clear is the CL1/CL2 pair. pdftotext of user-guide Table A.1 prints BL2 as 440W, while Porco et al. 2004 Table VIII and issna_inst.cat print 440M. Table A.1 prints WAC HAL as 656W; isswa_inst.cat prints 656N. pdftotext did not place a WAC numerical name on the Table A.1 MT2 row, but Table A.2 and isswa_inst.cat both include WAC MT2. The instrument catalog and the 2018 guide disagree on WAC spectral coverage (380-1050 nm versus 380-1100 nm). The WAC catalog overview says the wheels move at 3 positions per second, while its Filters section and Porco et al. 2004 say 2 positions per second in the WAC and 3 in the NAC. Figure A.6 of the user guide gives CCD quantum efficiency in electrons per incident photon, so the cameras are photon-counting detectors; DetectorType was left unset. No opened PDS or NASA page supplied a required acknowledgement sentence. Citation requests were not copied into acknowledgements. ADS abstracts returned HTTP 405 or a human-verification page, so no bibcode was recorded. Springer returned a client-challenge page. SVO filter pages timed out or returned 404 and were not used. The suggested user-guide URL dated 160929 returned HTTP 404. The West et al. 2010 author PDF at boulder.swri.edu failed TLS certificate verification and was not opened, so that calibration paper is not in references. The GISS HTML abstract gives doi:10.1007/s11214-004-1456-7. The NASA licence page qualifies that sentence: it applies unless the data file is marked with a restrictive notice or license. Since 2026-10-26 the band names carry the PDS system transmission, column 2 of COISS_0011 calib/efficiency/systrans/<cam><filter1><filter2>_systrans.tab (QE x optics x filter1 x filter2, full 0.1 nm grid; DetectorType photon from document/theoretical_basis.tex eq. 1), and get no SVO record (svo_filterID null). SVO's copies, windows cut from those files, are kept as <band>_svo and point at SVO's IDs (rename map filter_expansion/renamed_filters_20261026_cassini.csv). manifest.json adds the CCD QE (ccdqe.tab), the optics (na_optics.tab / wa_optics.tab) and derived filter pairs. The PDS data set catalog gives CITATION_DESC "Porco, C.P., CASSINI ORBITER CALIBRATION ISSNA/ISSWA 2 EDR VERSION 4.3, CO_CAL_ISSNA/ISSWA_2_EDR_V4.3, 2019" (calds.cat).
